sentences.text:
Subhash Ranjan Kumar Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. on
22 May, 2023
Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma

Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:112024
Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 5321 of 2023
Applicant :- Subhash Ranjan Kumar Singh And Another

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ravi Prakash Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.0047 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406, 120-B, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Dhaulana,
District Hapur.
It is submitted that in this case applicants are innocent and have committed no offence.
It is further submitted that there is nothing on record to show the complicity of the applicants in the present case.

It is also submitted that all the offences said to be committed are punishable with sentence less Subhash Ranjan Kumar Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92519596/
1 than 7 years even though the Investigating Officer is trying to arrest the applicants, therefore, the applicants are under apprehension of imminent arrest.

entities.text: Subhash Ranjan Kumar Singh And Another vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In case, the applicants are released on bail,
they would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and urged that in this case all the offences said to have been committed by the applicants are punishable with sentence less than 7 years regarding which protection u/s 41A Cr.P.C. is available to the applicants, therefore, there is no any apprehension of arrest of the applicants by the police.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, it appears that all the offences said to be committed by the applicants are punishable with sentence less than 7 years regarding which protection u/s 41A Cr.P.C. is already available to the applicants, therefore, there may be no apprehension of arrest against the applicants by the police.

Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application is disposed of finally in view of the protection as provided u/s 41, 41A, 60A and interpreted by the Honble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273 and again reiterated in the case of Satender Antil vs.
Central Bureau of Investigation and another LL 2022 SC 577 decided on 11.07.2022 according to which the Investigating Agency is duty bound to comply with the mandate of Section 41 and 41-A Cr.P.C. and any dereliction of their part has to be brought to be notice of higher authorities by the courts followed by appropriate action.
Order Date :- 22.5.2023
